channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: First Human Trial to Slash Bad Cholesterol by 50% With One Injection of CRISPR Gene-Editing Therapy
item.description: A single CRISPR infusion cut harmful cholesterol by about half, and the effect held a full year later. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: After 8 years in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope finally opens its eyes
item.description: An X-ray telescope bound for Mercury took its first observations after eight years and is beating expectations. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 33 Kids Wrote Letters to a Wounded Veteran. 60 Years Later, His Son Is Searching to Thank Each One
item.description: A son is tracing 33 schoolchildren whose 1967 letters comforted his wounded father, to thank each of them. How you can help: Write a short note to someone whose kindness you never thanked. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Rhino Dung Paper Is How This Family Makes Money and Protects These Amazing Animals
item.description: A family turns rhino dung into paper, giving villagers an income that makes living rhinos worth protecting. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Every Tuesday, This Chef Cooks for 100 People in Need Using Random Food Bank Ingredients
item.description: A Toronto-area chef cooks a meal for 100 people in need every Tuesday from whatever the food bank has. How you can help: Donate unopened food or an hour of time to your local food bank. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: CERN scientists finally find evidence of a particle decay so rare it took 40 years to detect
item.description: CERN physicists found the first evidence of a decay so rare it took 40 years of searching to see. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Montreal Is Harnessing Soothing Ocean Sounds to Combat Traffic Noise
item.description: A Montreal pocket park plays soothing ocean sounds to soften the traffic noise around it. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites
item.description: Former colliery sites in Yorkshire are being restored as habitat for frogs, newts and lizards. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Add a small pond or log pile to your garden for amphibians. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: CAR-T therapy helps stiff person syndrome patients walk and work again
item.description: In a Mayo Clinic trial, CAR-T therapy helped people with stiff person syndrome walk and return to work. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: She Checked on Her ‘Loud’ Upstairs Neighbor, Inspiring Strangers to Raise More Than $100,000
item.description: One neighbour knocked on a door, and strangers raised over $109,000 for an 87-year-old living with Parkinson’s. How you can help: Check in on an older neighbour who lives alone. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Empire State Building Lit Up with Gold Marks Historic Milestone of NASA’s Voyager 1 This Week
item.description: Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth, nearly 50 years after launch, and New York lit up in gold for it. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Over 100 Cave Bear Skeletons Found in ‘Sensational’ Discovery by Alpine Guide
item.description: An alpine guide found a cave holding the skeletons of more than 100 extinct cave bears, now kept safe from looters. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
item.description: Five centuries-old baobabs dug up without permits were stopped at export and are being replanted. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: The Waterless, Hyper-Efficient Machines That Clean Clothes With Carbon Dioxide
item.description: New machines clean clothes with recycled carbon dioxide instead of water, using far less energy. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Bans cut two forever chemicals by 30 percent in England’s rivers
item.description: Bans have cut the two most toxic forever chemicals by about 30% in England’s rivers over ten years. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Students Fighting to Save Poached Plant Species That Only Exists Near Their Campus
item.description: Santa Clara University students are working to save a wildflower that grows only near their campus. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Plant native wildflowers that local pollinators feed on. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Siblings Build 430-Step ‘Sky Ladder’ for Their Mother Who Refuses to Live in the City
item.description: Grown children built a 430-step stairway up a mountainside by hand so their mother can reach home safely. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: This Blue Whale Population Grew 1,000% Since the End of Antarctic Whaling
item.description: Antarctic blue whales have grown from 418 to about 4,000 since commercial whaling there ended in 1973. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘Huge experiment in biogeography’: US offshore windfarms are creating artificial reefs
item.description: Offshore wind turbine bases off the US coast are turning into reefs full of new marine life. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: Scientists ‘Cure’ Deadly Brain Tumors in Every Mouse Tested with New Cancer Therapy
item.description: A new immune cell therapy cleared an aggressive childhood brain cancer in every mouse tested and kept it away. Evidence: Early research. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert
item.description: Stone tools show early humans lived beside lakes full of hippos in Arabia 125,000 years ago. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: US homelessness decline hits its steepest one-year drop in a decade
item.description: US homelessness fell over 6% in 2025, about 49,000 fewer people, the steepest drop in a decade. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: April Surac built NeuraSensa so art adapts to the people using it
item.description: A young designer built NeuraSensa so public art adjusts to the sensory needs of the people using it. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: West Coast’s First Ever Sea Turtle Hatchlings Released into the Pacific (LOOK)
item.description: Olive ridley hatchlings rescued from a storm-threatened nest became the first released on the US West Coast. How you can help: Keep beach lights low and give nesting turtles plenty of space. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Algeria Returns Kindness Shown by Kansans Who Welcomed its World Cup Team with the Trip of a Lifetime
item.description: Algeria flew in Kansas families who hosted its World Cup team and gave them a trip of a lifetime in return. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Warren Buffett Gives Away $5.5 Billion in Thanksgiving Gift, Saying Kindness Is Priceless
item.description: Warren Buffett gave away about $5.5 billion in shares to charity in his yearly Thanksgiving donation. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Largest Electric Bus Fleet in New York to Serve Bronx Neighborhood Elevated Asthma Rates
item.description: New York’s largest electric school bus fleet now runs in a South Bronx area with high childhood asthma. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Can this experimental orchard save the UK’s cider industry?
item.description: A Somerset orchard is testing apple varieties and natural methods to keep cider trees thriving as climate shifts. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: The Greek coastline cleanup that turned trash into a pollution map
item.description: Volunteers cleaning a Greek islet logged each piece of trash, turning the haul into a map of sea pollution. How you can help: Join a local beach or river cleanup and note what you collect. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: NASA is offering $1 million for bold ideas to help build a Moon base
item.description: NASA is offering $1 million to US students for ideas to help build the first permanent Moon base. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Hidden ecosystem: Scientists discover 245 animals living inside a single deep-sea rock
item.description: Scientists counted over 4,100 tiny animals living inside deep-sea metal nodules, a hidden ecosystem. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Can Barbershops Turn Trust Into Better Health for Black Men?
item.description: Barbershops are using the trust of their chairs to bring health checks to Black men who skip the doctor. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Book a routine blood pressure check if you have not had one this year. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Pupils fascinated by space get astronomy lesson
item.description: A Cambridge astronomer visited First Tower School to give space-loving pupils a lesson in astronomy. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: This Tourette’s wrist device cut tics by a quarter in a UK trial
item.description: A wrist device cut tics by a quarter on average in a UK trial of 121 people with Tourette’s. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
item.description: SpaceX caught part of its Starship rocket with mechanical arms, a step toward fully reusable rockets. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
item.description: Astronomers found a large icy world beyond Pluto that could become the sixth recognised dwarf planet. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Maui Is Becoming a Living Laboratory for Regenerative Tourism
item.description: After the 2023 fires, Maui is asking visitors to help restore land and culture instead of just sightseeing. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
item.description: AI made a bionic eye implant more precise at predicting the light shapes a blind man perceives. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
item.description: A familiar tropical butterfly turned out to be three species, one of them new to science. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Imagining the Mossy Cities of the Future
item.description: A German founder grows moss walls that cool and clean city air, starting from a fight to save one tree. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: Colleges are adding childcare, family rooms and flexible help so student parents can finish degrees. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing
item.description: In Juneau, Alaska, neighbours feed each other by sharing fish, game and garden harvests. How you can help: Share extra garden produce or a meal with a neighbour this week. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: ‘It’s all God’s creation’: farmers continue a ‘Jewishly inspired’ agrarian tradition
item.description: A growing number of Jewish Americans are finding community through small farms rooted in old traditions. Source: The Guardian Environment.
